column6: Worked the example: u = x/4 − x²/2 and x²/2 − 3x/4 + ¼ satisfy −u″ = ±1, match value 0 and slope −¼ at x = ½, u″ jumps −1 to 1 (C¹ not C²). But the boundary condition u(0) = u(1) = 0 was dropped, so "its solution" was not determined; added it.

Bullet 2: trace characterization of H¹₀ needs boundary regularity; added "(for a bounded domain with C¹ boundary)". Bullet 3: Cantor function has no weak derivative (distributional derivative is the Cantor measure), so "its weak derivative is not zero" was wrong; now "it has no weak derivative at all". Old text note: Explainer calls the Lax-Milgram proof "constructive", which is loose.
Worked it: u solves Laplace, u(x,0) = 0, u_y(x,0) = sin(nx)/n; at y = 1 sinh(n)/n² ≈ 1.18, 2.97, 110 for n = 1, 5, 10 while data amplitude falls 1, 0.2, 0.1. Heat-mode comparison correct.

Bullet 3: dropped qualifier; classical Dirichlet problem can fail to have a solution on irregular bounded domains (punctured disk), added "with smooth boundary". Bullet 4: absolute "Inverse problems and data assimilation are ill-posed" changed to "Many inverse problems and data-assimilation problems". Old text note: Q4 (Dirichlet well-posed "on a bounded domain", Perron existence) has the same missing boundary-regularity qualifier.
